definition: Sum of IC3 crime types classed as fraud: investment, BEC, tech support, confidence/romance, government impersonation, non-payment/non-delivery, credit card/check, real estate, lottery, employment, advance fee, overpayment, phishing/spoofing, identity theft, misrepresentation, re-shipping, auction, charity, health care
coverage_notes: Category rows summed by researcher; rows sum to 16.088bn vs headline 16.600bn (pre-2023 rows exceed total because some complaints carried several crime types; from 2023/2025 one crime type per complaint). Share of category sum = 85.6%
source_title: IC3 2024 Internet Crime Report (crime types by victim loss)
notes: Derived (grade A inputs). BEC counted as fraud. Phishing/spoofing and identity theft counted as fraud (could be argued either way; together <$0.6bn in any year).

measure: IC3 losses in hacking-type crime categories (derived sum)
definition: Sum of IC3 crime types classed as hacking: ransomware, personal data breach, corporate/data breach, malware/virus/scareware, botnet, computer intrusion, SIM swap, extortion, denial of service, hacktivist
coverage_notes: Share of category sum = 12.5%. 'Personal Data Breach' and 'Extortion' are mixed (much extortion is sextortion/email extortion, not intrusion). Narrow hacking (excl. personal data breach and extortion) = 0.414bn
source_title: IC3 2024 Internet Crime Report (crime types by victim loss)
notes: Derived. IC3 ransomware losses exclude lost business, remediation, etc. and are ~25x below on-chain ransom payments; hacking dollars are badly under-measured here.
